transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, I'm only here because my parents and HR pressured me to come, but I don't think I really need to be. I feel like I’m on the verge of being a legendary visionary in fashion and everyone else is just too small-minded to keep up with me. They just don't understand the level I'm operating on right now.
Have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people around you cannot perceive, or do you feel like someone is trying to influence or harm you?

Yes, actually. Late at night when I'm alone, I hear this clear male voice right next to my ear giving me advice and warning me about people at work. On top of that, I know for a fact that the big sneaker brands and my coworkers are tracking my phone to copy my ideas and shut me down before I get too powerful.

Do you feel that these voices and the sense of being tracked started only during this period where you've felt like a 'legendary visionary,' or have you experienced these things even when your mood and energy were much lower?

I've actually experienced them during my low points, too. Even when I was totally crashed, just lying in bed with zero energy and not caring about anything, I still heard that male voice warning me. I was still completely sure the brands were tracking my phone, even though I didn't feel hyped up or manic at all.

During those low points when you felt no energy and didn't care about anything, did you also experience a significant loss of interest in activities you usually enjoy, or did you have any thoughts that life was not worth living?

Yeah, I completely lost interest in everything during those times, to the point where I'd just stare at my shoes, refuse to shower, and ignore all my texts. I didn't have any thoughts of wanting to end my life, though. I just felt completely empty, numb, and totally drained of all my energy.

When you experienced those low, empty periods, did you have a period of at least two weeks where you felt that way most of the day, nearly every day, alongside other symptoms like changes in your appetite or sleep?
I'm not really sure about appetite changes or the exact daily timing of those low periods. I mostly just remember crashing, feeling completely numb, and staying in bed without caring about anything.
During those low, empty periods, did you experience other symptoms like trouble falling or staying asleep, or did you find yourself sleeping significantly more than usual?

I didn't really pay attention to my sleep patterns during those low times, so I'm not entirely sure. I just remember lying in bed staring at my shoes and feeling completely numb, without really tracking if I was sleeping too much or too little.
Looking back at those low, empty periods, did they typically last for several weeks at a time, or were they shorter episodes that cleared up relatively quickly?

They are definitely shorter dips compared to the long, high-energy stretches that take up most of my year. But they aren't super brief either—they still last for at least a couple of weeks at a time where I'm just stuck in bed. Even during those couple of weeks, I'm still hearing the voice and feeling like I'm being watched.

Beyond the voices and the feeling of being watched, have you experienced other symptoms like disorganized speech, trouble focusing, or a significant decline in your ability to take care of your daily personal hygiene or work tasks over the past six months or longer?

Yes, I've definitely struggled with those. When I'm talking, I jump from one idea to another so fast that people can't keep up, and during my low periods, I stop showering, ignore texts, and completely neglect my work by blowing deadlines and walking out mid-shift. All of this has been going on for over a year, ever since I got my promotion.

Thinking about the past year, have the periods where you feel high-energy and 'visionary' lasted for a significant portion of the total time you've been experiencing these symptoms, or do the psychotic symptoms (the voice and the feeling of being tracked) persist for most of the time regardless of your mood?

Both of those things are actually happening. The high-energy, "visionary" phases have taken up the vast majority of this past year, with only those short periods of crashing in between. But even during those low, numb times when I had no energy, the voice in my ear and the feeling that I was being tracked by the brands still persisted the whole time.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports that psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions) persist even during periods of low mood/energy, and that these symptoms have been present for over a year. This suggests that the psychosis is not exclusively occurring during mood episodes, which makes a primary mood disorder with psychotic features less likely. The persistence of psychosis independent of mood supports F20.0 (Schizophrenia) or F25.0 (Schizoaffective disorder, manic type), as the patient describes significant manic-like 'visionary' phases as well as depressive 'crashes'. F25.1 is now less likely because the patient describes the high-energy/manic phases as taking up the 'vast majority' of the year, rather than depressive phases.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and paranoid delusions) that continue during periods of low mood/energy when no mood symptoms are present. Because the psychotic symptoms are present independently of the mood episodes for a significant duration, and the psychotic symptoms are the primary, continuous feature, F20.0 (Schizophrenia) is the most appropriate diagnosis over Schizoaffective disorder.
